covered: the in-flight percentage the operator sees is required to be the transfer's actual progress rather than a placeholder. A weight transfer is held mid-file with 65536 bytes of a larger payload delivered, the detail panel is opened on that record, and the progress bar it renders is required to agree with the numbers the API reports for the same instant: the bar must equal the truncation of the API percentage and must be strictly between 0 and 100, so it cannot claim a finished transfer while the file is still arriving. Both numbers are recorded - at the held instant the API reports 78.127 percent and the bar renders 78 - so the claim rests on the pair rather than on an absence of errors. Completion is still asserted separately, with the exact hundred and the success mark. This closes the gap that a bar pinned to 100 everywhere used to pass. Proven by mutation: replacing the percent with a constant 100 fails with the bar and the reported progress named side by side.

covered by this case for the disconnect-and-resume half, at byte level: one transfer is cut mid-body (interrupted true, 65536 of 524310 bytes), and the run then records four subsequent GETs with exact Range headers - the gap at 1572930-2097239 and the three remaining windows - each compared against the bytes it claims to send, ending in a complete file whose sha256 matches. Resumption is proven by the ranges, not inferred from the row turning green.

Both clauses are proven, in the same run. First clause: a real transfer is started to an owned local storage from the model detail Download to dialog and the source is held mid-response, so the row is genuinely downloading with real bytes on disk. The page's own row-level Cancel download control is used: it opens the presenceAction.cancelDownloadConfirm popconfirm, and confirming it is asserted to send exactly one POST /api/v1/models/{id}/download/cancel carrying storage_id and node_uuid and nothing else, answered 200 with state canceled. The presenceMessage.downloadCanceled toast appears, the row renders the presence.canceled label together with the row reason, and an independent GET of the model agrees on state canceled, acquisition download and the message Download canceled by user. The bytes already reported are neither zeroed nor inflated to the finished total by the withdrawal, so the row cannot pass the cancel off as a completed transfer. Termination is asserted against the task and not against the label: the source's held response is then torn down under the agent, and for a five second window afterwards the source receives no further request at all, while the row stays canceled. The temporary resource is asserted too: the resumable weight-name .part file survives the cancel at the exact full weight size carrying payload bytes while the finished weight file does not exist, which is what the confirm text promises for a retry. The temporary resource is further pinned to real data: the chunk writer preallocates the full size and fills chunks out of order, so every byte the transfer did write is compared against the source payload at that same offset and any mismatch would fail the case, which rules out a sparse hole being passed off as a resume point. Proven by mutation: the withdrawal was made label-only by removing the writer stop call and by no longer pausing the task for a canceled row, and the cancel test then failed with AssertionError: the canceled transfer kept asking the source for bytes: ... range bytes=1638466-2097239 ... so the five second window is not a tautology and the canceled row cannot be relabelled while the transfer keeps running. Finally the row is reclaimed and the eviction answers a physical byte count equal to the count the canceled row reported, so the kept data is accounted for. Second clause: the pre-submit Download to dialog is reopened and Cancel, Escape, close cross and mask are each taken with zero POST /download requests and no file row created, so closing the dialog is a dialog dismissal and not a task cancellation; this is asserted separately from the row cancel above.

covered: the transfer is still held at the source barrier when the page is reloaded, so the background task has to be read back rather than restarted. The independent GET issued by the reload returns 200 with the same row still downloading and the same byte count as before it, and the reopened detail renders the same bar value it rendered before the reload - 78 against 1638685 of 2097459 bytes in both runs - so a reload that zeroed the progress or reported the task finished cannot pass. The reopened panel is asserted visible with exactly one file row, and the source is released only afterwards so the transfer completes from the held position.
covered for the files this case transfers: the reassembled payload is hashed at an independent agent root after the resumed ranges complete, so the resumed result is verified end to end.

Partial: only the download side applies to this surface, and this case proves the bytes and format half of it after an interrupted transfer resumes. Each delivered file on the actual chosen path is decoded through its own standard envelope - config.json by Python's json module, model.safetensors by the length-prefixed header the safetensors format defines - and the sha256 of the bytes on disk equals the sha256 of the bytes the external repository served, so the resumed artifact is verified as the declared format and as byte-identical content rather than as a resent document. The directory is then enumerated: it holds exactly the source file set beside the product's own completion marker, whose measured byte total equals the sum of the served files, with no .part, .part.state, .tmp or .html leftover from the interruption, which is the specific risk this case creates. The clause that a failure must not download an HTML error page as the file is NOT claimed by this case, because this case does not make the source fail; that clause is proven on the failure-retry case, which really refuses the weight with a 503 and calibrates the HTML detector against the fixture's real error body. The export-shaped sub-dimensions are also NOT claimed: 中文编码, 列/单位, 记录数与筛选一致 require an exported artifact, and this page has none - neither models locale file contains any word for export, ui/src/pages/models has no export surface, the tables declare no antd filter or sorter, and the backend exposes no model export route. That half belongs to the logs export contract, declared there by log-filter-export.json; claiming it here would be a mis-attribution, so this item remains a gap in the completion queue.
